draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Ooty! The Queen of hill stations sits at 2,240 m in the Nilgiris, and back in British times it served as the summer capital of the Madras Presidency. Its official name, Udhagamandalam, comes from a Toda word meaning 'house in mountains'.
draft.hungryLine: Most places here serve South Indian food, and since the Nilgiris are famous for tea, a hot cup is never a bad idea.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Holy Trinity Church is just a 2 min walk away, and Adam's fountain at Charring Cross is about 9 minutes. Keep going to the busy Ooty Municipal Market, 11 minutes on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Stroll up to the Government Rose Garden on the slopes of Elk Hill, a 15 min walk. Or head to the lake for a lazy paddle boat ride.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Ooty was one of the first places in India to get rid of plastic carry bags, so bring your own reusable bag.

spots.name: Holy Trinity Church
spots.detail: 2 min walk · A chapel for Tamil Christians that was dedicated as a church in 1858

spots.name: Ooty Municipal Market
spots.detail: 11 min walk · Built in 1848, one of India's biggest retail markets, great for fresh fruit

spots.name: Government Rose Garden
spots.detail: 15 min walk · Rose park on the slopes of Elk Hill at 2,200 m

legends.title: House in the mountains
legends.body: The Todas, one of the hill tribes who lived here first, gave the town its name from 'othakal-mund', meaning house in mountains. That became Udhagamandalam, and the British shortened it all the way to Ooty.

legends.title: The goddess of rain
legends.body: Mariamman is the local deity of the region, and her temple sits near the market. She's the goddess of rain, which makes a lot of sense up in these misty hills.

tips.title: Carry a reusable bag.
tips.body: Ooty did away with plastic carry bags early, so bring your own for shopping.

tips.title: Pack a light layer.
tips.body: Days here hover around a pleasant 20 to 25 °C all year, a nice escape from the heat down on the plains.

story.title: Hill tribes' home
story.body: The Nilgiri Mountains show up as early as Tamil Sangam literature. The region was home to hill tribes like the Badagas, Todas, Kotas, Irulas and Kurumbas.

story.title: A sanatorium by a lake
story.body: The East India Company took control in the 18th century. In the early 19th century the British built Ooty up as a sanatorium around an artificial lake.

story.title: A hill town takes shape
story.body: The municipal market opened in 1848, Holy Trinity Church was dedicated in 1858, and Ooty became a municipality in 1866. Adam's fountain went up at Charring Cross in 1886.

story.title: Summer capital
story.body: Ooty served as the summer capital of the Madras Presidency. Breeks Memorial School opened in 1874 and Sacred Heart Cathedral was built in 1897.

story.title: Queen of hill stations
story.body: After independence, Ooty grew into a favourite hill station, living on tourism and farming. The Nilgiri Mountain Railway still links it to the plains.
